title: Sun, Earth and Moon
prompt: a brass orrery of the Sun, Earth and Moon on geared arms with a lamp in the Sun: run a month and watch the Moon's phases on a small phase dial, step to a solar eclipse with the Moon's shadow falling on Earth, step to a lunar eclipse with the Moon in Earth's shadow, tilt the Moon's orbit to show why eclipses are rare; see-through shows the gear train and the shadow cones
blurb: Turn a brass teaching orrery through a lunar month and compare eclipse alignments with a tilted orbit, with enlarged bodies and distances that are not to astronomical scale.
teachingNotes: Original bench apparatus. Sun-Earth direction is fixed for one 29.53-day phase cycle. The Sun globe encloses a small lamp. Shadow cones follow that lamp, not the globe's outer radius. Eclipse controls level the orbit to demonstrate a node alignment. Tilt is 5.1 degrees with nodes perpendicular to the lamp direction; orbit height is exaggerated fourfold as shown in the tilt readout. No annual motion, node precession or atmospheric reddening is simulated.
